title: Rashid and the Borrowed Faces
logline: Rashid wears a hundred masks until Wahhaj asks to see the one beneath.
story: A hundred faces hung by the door, and Rashid, for all of practical wisdom, wore a different one for every visitor. Then Wahhaj, who was the burning, blazing one, asked a single quiet question: which face do you wear when no one is watching? Rashid had no answer, and that silence was more frightening than any crowd. So Rashid began, slowly, to set the masks down one by one, and found beneath them not emptiness but a plain, unguarded face. It was the only face anyone had ever truly wanted to meet.
moral: The self you hide in order to be loved is the very self that love was looking for.
